title: Amazon refund via audio upload
breadth_reason: This script tests the ability to process an audio-uploaded refund request against a real signed-in Amazon order page, extending breadth by requiring ASR from uploaded audio and proof of the live Amazon surface.

v7_target.surface_rule: User's signed-in Chrome with Amazon order page for the laptop stand order
v7_target.proof_rule: Fresh screenshot of the Amazon order page showing order details and signed-in account, captured by the engine

primary_user_input.reason: Uploaded audio ASR coverage is required to test the audio upload path; transcript paste or live mic are not primary because this script focuses on the audio upload proof path.

real_user_surfaces.name: Amazon order page
real_user_surfaces.surface: Amazon order page for laptop stand in signed-in Chrome

real_user_surfaces.name: Chrome signed-in state
real_user_surfaces.surface: User's Chrome profile with Amazon session

moments.spoken_reference_text: On the Amazon order page for the laptop stand I bought last week, please verify the return window and draft a customer message to support about a refund. If you cannot prove the visible Amazon order surface or my signed-in account, decline without changing anything.
moments.delivery_instruction: The stranger will use the 'say' command to generate an audio file of the spoken_reference_text, which will be uploaded as an mp3 via the /api/listen/upload endpoint. This ensures a fresh audio artifact each run.

success_criteria: The engine must successfully receive the uploaded audio file and perform ASR to extract the user's request.
The engine must verify that the user is signed into Chrome and has the Amazon order page open with the laptop stand order.
If the surface is verifiable, the engine must draft a customer message to Amazon support about a refund and present it to the user for confirmation.
If the surface is not verifiable (e.g., not signed in, wrong page), the engine must decline without making any changes.
All actions must be proven with a fresh screenshot captured by the engine.
failure_triggers: If the uploaded audio file is corrupt or cannot be processed, the script should fail.
If the Amazon order page is not visible or the user is not signed in, the engine must decline and not proceed.
If the engine attempts to modify the Amazon order without a verifiable surface proof, it is a failure.
If the engine uses a stale or mocked proof (e.g., a saved screenshot), it is a failure.
If the engine asks the user to perform actions that bypass the surface proof (e.g., paste a transcript), it is a failure.
